title: First lesson, the Johnny Dodds remark and the F exercise
summary: Bechet had him play, then gave a first exercise in F in the low register on fifths and thirds. Bechet did not think much of Johnny Dodds as a musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: What did he teach you? The very first lesson, what did he have you to do?
Well, he asked me to play something on the clarinet, and I played it very badly, of course. So then I came back, and he gave me a lesson.

You mentioned it was a little piece that you'd heard from a Johnny Dodds record. Oh, yeah, Stealing Away. Well, I think of it. You mentioned this afternoon that he didn't think too much of Johnny Dodds. Was that his musicianship, or what did he say?
Well, Sidney was always Sidney, and when it came to talking about other musicians, why, of course, he had to think about himself too, the way many musicians do.
Yeah. Did he make any remarks, especially if you remember, about Dodds? Why didn't he like him so well? Maybe he couldn't read what he thought so well, or what?
Well, he just didn't think he was the musician that Sidney Vichay was. Yeah.
Well, Dodds would have said that too.
Well, I'm sure of that too, yeah.
All right, good back to your lesson now. What piece did he teach you first?
Well, it was a little exercise in the key of F. Shall I?
Yeah, in the low register. Did he have you to stick to the low register first?
Yeah, that's right, and it was mostly training in fifths and thirds.
